messages:
maria.g: hey folks, I'm stuck accepting the org invite. it says the invite email is linked to a different GitHub account. has anyone run into this?
ashwin: welcome! yes, that happens if your browser is signed into your personal GH account while clicking the invite. did you use the invite email link or try to accept from the org page?
katie: @maria.g can you paste the exact error text from the browser or email? sometimes the message tells us which account it expects.
maria.g: browser message: 'This invitation was sent to maria@redwood.com, which is linked to a different GitHub account. To join the organization, sign out of that account and accept the invitation from the invite link.'
onboarding-bot: Hi Maria 44b3fb - the onboarding doc has a troubleshooting section for invite conflicts: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/github
julian: two practical routes: 1) remove your work email from your personal GitHub account (Settings -> Emails), sign out, then open the invite link and sign in with SSO; 2) ask an org admin to resend the invite to a different email alias if you want to keep the work email on your personal account.
maria.g: i'm nervous about removing the work email from my personal account - will that break PR attribution or notifications?
julian: (typo) julian: it won't affect PRs or repo ownership. it only removes the email as a login/notification address. make sure you have at least one verified email on the personal account before removing the work one.
ashwin: alternative quick workaround: open the invite link in a private/incognito window, accept it, then sign in with SSO when prompted. also clear cookies if needed.
maria.g: tried incognito, but the SSO option doesn't show at login, it only offers username/password.
julian: (typo) julian: SSO shows when your email is associated with the org; if it doesn't, the invite acceptance flow should prompt. if it's not, we can reissue the invite after unlinking.
maria.g: ok I'll remove the work email from my personal account now. can someone resend the invite after?
ashwin: i can resend once you confirm. steps for folks: 1) remove work email from personal account; 2) sign out of all GH sessions or use incognito; 3) click the invite link; 4) sign in via SSO or the 'Sign in with SSO' option.
maria.g: removed the work email and accepted the invite successfully 389. thanks! i'm in the org but don't see the serving-runtime repo yet. i selected 'infra' team on the invite flow.
ashwin: team membership sometimes lags a minute. i'll add you to infra/team-devs (write) and docs (write) now. also, make sure you add an SSH key if you need CI access: `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "maria@redwood.com"` then paste the public key into github.com/settings/ssh/new.
julian: FYI we require org members to enable two-factor auth. set that up under Settings -> Security -> Two-factor authentication, and save your recovery codes to 1Password.
maria.g: i've set up 2FA but misplaced the recovery codes during setup. where should i store them?
katie: add them to the company vault (1Password) under a secure item and also keep an encrypted local copy. security policy: https://redwood.dev/security/2fa.
ashwin: i've added you to infra/team-devs and the repos now - you should see redwood/serving-runtime and redwood/console. try cloning and ping if any permissions errors.
maria.g: can clone and push a test branch, all good. huge thanks everyone! :heart:
devops-bot: Reminder: complete the GitHub onboarding checklist to pass automated access audits: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/checklist
ashwin: if you run into anything else DM me or ping #new-hires. welcome aboard!
